summary: Redwood AE + SE walked Cerulean Health team through hosted embeddings + reranking workflow using Redwood API and Console. Demonstrated embeddings ingestion, semantic search baseline, then reranker endpoint to improve precision for the top-K results. Discussed latency/cost tradeoffs, streaming vs non-streaming, caching, token economics, and security (SOC2, SSO, data retention). Customer is evaluating hosted API first with a short pilot; requested pricing, SSO docs, and a benchmark run on their sample data.
topics: Intro & goals; current stack & pain; demo: embeddings ingest -> vector DB flow -> search -> reranker call; Console walkthrough for routes & analytics; Optimize suggestions (batching, quantization); security & compliance questions; next steps.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-05
Start time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Owen Patel (Redwood SE), Nina Rosario (Head of Search, Cerulean), Devon Lee (ML Eng, Cerulean), Samir Khan (CTO, Cerulean)

00:00 Nina: Hey everyone, uh thanks for making time. We wanted to focus on embeddings+rerank today — we've been getting noisy search results from our current vector pipeline and want to see how Redwood's hosted stuff can help.
00:12 Maya: Great — thanks Nina. Quick intro, I'm Maya, I'm the AE; Owen here is our SE, he'll drive the walkthrough. Can I confirm your main success metric? Is it lift in top-3 precision or reducing false positives?
00:26 Nina: Top-3 precision is primary, but latency under 400ms on average for the search flow is also important for product. We do trials with a couple of thousand queries/day initially.
00:38 Owen: Thanks. Do you currently use an external vector DB? Pinecone? OpenSearch? Or an in-house index?
:42 Samir: We're on an older in-house retriever, elastic + custom tf-idf + a cheap vector store that sits on S3; it's a bit messy.
00:50 Owen: Ok got it — that explains some of the noise. We'll demo a hosted API flow where you can push embeddings into your pipeline, run a nearest-neighbor retrieval to get top-K, and then call our reranker endpoint to reorder those top-K using a cross-encoder style model.
01:05 Nina: Sounds good. Cost is a factor — if reranking every result is costly, can we do partial rerank or only on the top 5?
01:13 Owen: Absolutely. Common production pattern: retrieve top-50 via fast ANN, then rerank top-5 or top-10. That preserves latency and limits token/compute cost. We'll show the console settings for that.
01:24 Maya: Quick note, Cerulean — since you're evaluating hosted: we have Redwood Optimize recommendations which will suggest batch sizes and rerank thresholds based on your workload to hit cost/latency targets.
01:35 Devon: How invasive is it to switch? We can't rewrite everything in a week.
01:39 Owen: Good question. For hosted API, you can keep your existing index and just call Redwood reranker as a downstream service — minimal changes. Alternatively, use our embeddings endpoint to recompute vectors and store them where you want. We have SDK snippets for Python/Node.
02:00 [30s pause / screen share transitions]
02:12 Owen: Ok sharing my screen — I'll run through a quick example using our demo dataset. First step: ingest text -> call /v1/embeddings to get vectors. Here's a sample curl and Python snippet.
02:30 Owen (screen): curl -X POST /v1/embeddings -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-001","input":["doc text 1","doc text 2"]}'
02:40 Owen: One gotcha we've seen in transcripts is mismatch in chunking. If you chunk shorter than your semantic window you lose context; if too long you hurt retrieval recall. Our Optimize tab will recommend chunk sizes based on your queries.
03:02 Nina: Can you show the console where those embeddings show up?
03:07 Owen: Yep — Console -> Data -> Embeddings. Here you can see ingestion logs, sample vectors, and token counts. Note: hosted embeddings are ephemeral unless you wire them to a backstore; many teams upload vectors to their vector DB but use Redwood to compute and rerank.
03:30 Devon: On the reranker itself — what model family? Is it a cross-encoder?
03:36 Owen: It's a cross-encoder style model tuned for reranking; we expose it as a rerank endpoint that takes the top-K candidate ids and the query and returns scores + reordered list. Example payload in the demo: {"query":"...","candidates":[{"id":"123","text":"..."}, ... ]}.
03:52 Nina: The demo just showed text fields; how do you handle passing metadata like doc type or embargoed flags?
03:58 Owen: You can include metadata in the candidate objects and we surface it for scoring logic. We also support filtering before rerank at query time.
04:12 [timestamped silence, typing noises]
04:25 Owen: Alright I'll run a baseline: retrieve top-50 via FAISS on local dev set, then call reranker for top-5. Watch the timing — retrieval is ~90ms, rerank call in hosted mode is about 120ms for 5 candidates on this model size. So end-to-end 210-230ms in this demo environment.
05:02 Nina: That's promising. What's the cost per rerank call roughly? ballpark per 1k requests?
05:08 Maya: I'll give you conservative hosted numbers: reranking top-5 on this model roughly equates to X token-equivalents — for quick ballpark, it's in the tens of dollars per 1k queries depending on model size; we'll send an exact sheet. Optimize helps you find the cheaper model or quantized variant.
05:29 Nina: Can you do streaming outputs for rerank? We want to show progress to users for long queries.
05:34 Owen: Rerank is synchronous and returns scores; streaming is more for decoder generation. You could stream a partial UI while retrieval completes, but reranker itself is a fast point-call.
05:46 Samir: How does caching work? If we see repeated queries, will that reduce cost?
05:50 Owen: Yes — we have prefix and query caching; for exact repeated query rerank results can be cached and served from edge. Our console shows cache hit rates. For semantic similarity, cache hit rates are lower but worth caching normalized queries or intents.
06:08 Devon: Security questions — is data persisted in Redwood? We have strict data residency & HIPAA-ish requirements for patient notes.
06:18 Maya: Important. Hosted default keeps transient logs and we can offer configurable retention; SOC2 attestation is available. For regulated data many customers choose Redwood Private or Dedicated. We also have KMS integrations and SSO/SAML for access control. I'll attach our security whitepaper.
06:38 Nina: Would pilot forced to Private? We're trying hosted first, but we might require no-PHI in pilot.
06:45 Samir: We're open to hosted for non-PHI only. For PHI we'd need Private or dedicated with audit logs.
06:51 Maya: Understood. We can scope pilot with anonymized data.
07:00 [screen: Console Routes view]
07:10 Owen: Here's a sample API route configuration: you can set model fallback policies, define max tokens, set rerank threshold, and TTL for cache. The Console also has per-route latency histograms.
07:35 Owen: Now I'm going to run two variants: rerank top-5 using the smaller optimized model vs larger high-accuracy model — compare precision@3 and latency.
07:50 Owen (typing): Variant A (small): avg rerank latency 95ms, p@3 0.62. Variant B (large): latency 170ms, p@3 0.73. So about 10% absolute lift on p@3 at cost of ~80ms.
08:20 Nina: That's the tradeoff we expected. Is there an A/B rollout support so we can test in production?
08:27 Owen: Yes — Console supports canary and A/B routing per route; you can compare metrics and auto-fallback if latency spikes.
08:36 Devon: How do we measure regression in relevance over time?
08:40 Owen: We have Eval suites — you upload labeled queries and we compute regression alerts. Optimize can tie alerts to prompt sets. We'll demo that in the CSM flow.
08:55 [noise/crosstalk as screen is switched]
09:10 Nina: A few practical questions: we have multi-tenant product — can we partition by tenant so embeddings don't leak?
09:18 Maya: Yes — you can namespace embeddings and restrict via RBAC. For hosted, we enforce isolation at the tenant config level; for Dedicated/Private you get stronger network isolation.
09:30 Samir: SSO — SAML? SCIM for provisioning?
09:33 Maya: We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for user sync. Will include docs.
09:40 Devon: Okay, can you show an example Python snippet for rerank?
09:44 Owen: Sure — pasted in chat:
09:48 Owen (screen): from redwood import Client
09:50 Owen (screen): client = Client(api_key='REDACTED')
09:53 Owen (screen): resp = client.rerank.query(query_text, candidates=list_of_candidates, top_k=5)
09:58 Owen: The response includes scores and you can map back to your document ids.
10:08 Nina: Are there limits on request size for candidate lists?
10:12 Owen: Practical limit is 200-500 candidates before performance degrades; we recommend ANN retrieval then rerank top 5-20.
10:20 [20s typing pause]
10:40 Owen: Quick dive into Optimize tab — here we run workload analysis and give config diffs: batching, recommended model, quantization level, recommended cache TTL. For your workload with many short queries, Optimize would suggest smaller batch sizes and aggressive prefix caching.
11:05 Nina: Does Optimize handle embeddings recompute costs if we change chunking?
11:09 Owen: It simulates cost impact of re-chunking and suggests best tradeoff given your SLA.
11:20 Maya: Anything on legal/procurement?
11:23 Samir: We need indemnities and data processing addendum. We'll start procurement after pilot if numbers look good.
11:33 Maya: We'll hand over legal contact and DPA template.
11:37 Devon: On instrumentation — can we get token-level cost breakdown?
11:41 Owen: Yes — Console shows token consumption per route + per-call breakdown. Good for cost attribution.
11:52 Nina: One more real-world ask — sometimes reranker brings in subtle hallucinations by over-weighting certain features; can we do guardrails?
11:59 Owen: We support constraint tokens and hard filters before scoring; also post-rerank heuristics. We recommend human-in-the-loop validation during rollout.
12:12 [presenter pauses; file transfer in chat — sample dataset link]
12:30 Nina: We'll share a small anonymized corpus and 500 labeled queries. Expect that tomorrow.
12:36 Owen: Great — once we have that Owen will run the 1k-query sim and share per-query lat/cost + p@3 numbers.
12:44 Maya: To recap: we'll send pricing + SSO/SOC2 docs, Owen will run rerank benchmark on your sample, Devon to share data, then we schedule a pilot kickoff.
12:55 Samir: Sounds good. Anything else?
13:00 Nina: No, that's it. Thanks for the practical runthrough.
13:04 [meeting ends]
notes: Customer prefers hosted pilot with anonymized data due to PHI concerns; Private considered for production.
Demo numbers: small model p@3 0.62 @95ms; large model p@3 0.73 @170ms — tradeoff discussed.
Optimize recommendations will be used to set batch sizes and chunking for pilot.
